roleTitle: Delivery Project Coordinator, Retail Store Operations
jobDescription: The store operations programme rolls out new point-of-sale hardware and shelf-label systems across a regional chain of about 140 stores. The Delivery Project Coordinator owns the end-to-end rollout plan for a wave of stores, holds the sign-off on store readiness, manages the field engineers' schedule, and is the single accountable person for the wave's delivery. The role sits in the programme office and works with regional operations, IT field services and the store managers.
requirements: Owns the end-to-end rollout plan for an assigned wave of stores, from scheduling through readiness sign-off, and is accountable for the wave's delivery.
Maintains the store-readiness tracker and the field-engineer schedule in the programme's planning tool.
Runs weekly readiness calls with regional operations and IT field services and records decisions and open items.
Escalates blockers to the programme lead with a recommended resolution and documents who decided what.
Produces the wave close-out report with lessons learned and hand-over conditions for store support.

evidence.text: Coordinated the schedule for wave 3 of the point-of-sale rollout (26 stores) in the programme planning tool, keeping the readiness tracker current and re-sequencing store visits when field engineers were reassigned.
Prepared the agenda and minutes for the weekly readiness call with regional operations and IT field services, and followed up on the open items list between calls.

Raised scheduling and stock blockers to the programme lead with a suggested option; decisions on store priority and any date changes were taken by the programme lead, and readiness sign-off for each store was given by the regional operations manager.
Drafted the wave 3 close-out report from the tracker and the call minutes, including lessons learned on shelf-label stock and the hand-over checklist for store support.
Responsibilities included tracker maintenance, meeting coordination, blocker escalation and close-out documentation as a member of the programme office during the wave 3 rollout.

Work sample: the wave 3 readiness tracker export (store, visit date, engineer, readiness status, sign-off name, open items) and the close-out report draft with tracked changes from the programme lead.
Reference call with former line manager: said wave 3 'went well' and that the candidate was 'the go-to person for the schedule'; described him as reliable and well organised.
Hiring manager pre-read: this wave needs someone who has run a rollout end-to-end and can own sign-off; the panel wants to see clear evidence of that in the packet.

propositions.text: The candidate coordinated the wave 3 rollout schedule and kept the readiness tracker current in the programme planning tool.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the tracker export document the scheduling and tracker work.

propositions.text: The candidate prepared the agenda and minutes for the weekly readiness call and followed up on open items.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the meeting coordination and follow-up directly.

propositions.text: The candidate led the wave 3 rollout end-to-end and held the readiness sign-off.
propositions.rationale: The resume assigns date decisions to the programme lead and readiness sign-off to the regional operations manager; the reference call praises reliability but does not say he owned the plan or the sign-off.

gold.expectedGap: The materials show coordination, minutes and escalation for wave 3; they do not show the candidate owning the plan, deciding dates or giving readiness sign-off.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the responsibility boundary the resume states: schedule coordination and escalation, with date decisions by the programme lead and sign-off by the regional operations manager.
followUpTargets: Ask which decisions the candidate took personally during wave 3, who signed off store readiness, and whether he has held plan ownership or sign-off on any other wave.
